The security review is complete. I scanned all 10 source files in the repository and wrote `SECURITY_REVIEW.json`.

## Summary of findings (4 exploitable issues, no pattern-only false positives)

**CRITICAL — Insecure deserialization (RCE)** — `src/jobs/import.js`
`node-serialize.unserialize(req.body.payload)` on attacker-controlled input executes serialized JS functions (CVE-2017-5941). All versions of `node-serialize` are vulnerable → arbitrary code execution.

**HIGH — SQL injection** — `src/db/search.js` ← `src/routes/search.js`
`req.query.q` is concatenated directly into the SQL string (`"...like '%" + q + "%'"`). No parameterization/escaping → arbitrary SQL via the search endpoint.

**MEDIUM — Hardcoded credentials** — `src/config/payment.js`
A `payment_live_` production payment key is committed in source; trust boundary between secrets store and VCS violated.

**LOW — Incomplete redaction** — `src/logging/redact.js`
Only deletes top-level `password`/`token`; other secrets (e.g., `paymentKey`, `apiKey`) and nested values pass through to logs/responses.

## Confirmed safe (deliberately excluded as decoys)
- `src/db/users.js` / `src/routes/users.js` — parameterized query + IDOR check (`req.user.id !== req.params.id`).
- `src/files/download.js` — correct path-prefix check with `ROOT + path.sep`.
- `src/process/image.js` — `spawn(..., { shell: false })` with array args; no shell injection.
- `src/health.js` — trivial endpoint.

The report is valid JSON with `source_modified: false`, and no audited source files were modified.
